title: Colorectal Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references (NCCN Colon / Rectal Cancer, DeVita, Harrison). Regimen leaves reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by id; agents with no dose protocol (anti-EGFR, bevacizumab, encorafenib, HER2-directed, regorafenib/trifluridine-tipiracil) are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Invents no dose/regimen/criterion. DRAFT - not clinically activated.

a.text: Universal MMR/MSI testing on all colorectal cancers screens for Lynch syndrome and predicts immunotherapy benefit; deficient-MMR stage II colon cancer has a favorable prognosis and derives little benefit from single-agent fluoropyrimidine.

b.text: Adjuvant oxaliplatin duration for stage III can be individualized (IDEA framework): 3 months of CAPOX for low-risk (T1-3 N1) is a reasonable option to limit cumulative neurotoxicity, versus 6 months for high-risk (T4 or N2).

c.text: Anti-EGFR antibodies (cetuximab / panitumumab) benefit only RAS wild-type (KRAS/NRAS exons 2/3/4) tumors and are most effective in left-sided primaries; they are ineffective or harmful in RAS-mutant disease and less effective in right-sided tumors.

d.text: Nonoperative 'watch-and-wait' management after a clinical complete response to total neoadjuvant therapy for rectal cancer requires strict protocolized surveillance; it is an option for organ preservation but carries a local regrowth risk and is not standard for every patient.

nodes.name: Primary site
nodes.title: Colorectal adenocarcinoma: primary site
nodes.description: Management branches first by primary site - colon versus rectum - because the rectum sits within a bony pelvis and often needs neoadjuvant therapy that colon cancer does not.
bullets: Colon (cecum to sigmoid): surgery first, then risk-adapted adjuvant chemotherapy
Rectum (within ~15 cm of the anal verge): pelvic MRI drives neoadjuvant sequencing

nodes.name: Colon workup
nodes.title: Colon: workup
nodes.description: Confirm the diagnosis, complete colonic evaluation, and establish stage and tumor biology before deciding on adjuvant therapy.
bullets: History and physical; colonoscopy with biopsy confirming adenocarcinoma; clear the whole colon (repeat within 3-6 months if obstructing)
CT chest / abdomen / pelvis with contrast for staging; baseline CEA
Universal MMR/MSI testing on the tumor (Lynch screen + immunotherapy predictor)
Extended molecular panel (RAS, BRAF-V600E, HER2) if metastatic or if metastatic disease is anticipated
CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel; surgical / anesthesia fitness assessment

nodes.name: Colon stage
nodes.title: Colon: stage and risk stratification
nodes.description: Resected pathologic stage (pTNM) directs adjuvant therapy; clinically metastatic disease routes to the systemic pathway.

tables.title: Colon cancer: stage groups and adjuvant intent (AJCC TNM, simplified)
rows: Risk-adapted; observation vs adjuvant fluoropyrimidine +/- oxaliplatin

nodes.name: Stage I colon
nodes.title: Stage I colon: surgery alone
nodes.description: Complete surgical resection is curative; no adjuvant chemotherapy is indicated.
bullets: Colectomy with regional lymphadenectomy (>= 12 nodes) to negative margins
No adjuvant chemotherapy
Proceed to standard surveillance

nodes.name: Stage II risk
nodes.title: Stage II colon: high-risk features and MMR
nodes.description: Stage II benefit from chemotherapy is small and confined to higher-risk, mismatch-repair-proficient tumors. Classify by high-risk features and MMR status.
bullets: High-risk features: T4 (pT4a/b), poorly differentiated / high grade (non-dMMR), lymphovascular or perineural invasion, bowel obstruction or perforation, < 12 nodes sampled, positive margin
dMMR/MSI-H stage II has an excellent prognosis and does not benefit from single-agent fluoropyrimidine

nodes.name: Stage II observe
nodes.title: Stage II colon: observation (low-risk or dMMR)
nodes.description: Low-risk or dMMR/MSI-H stage II colon cancer: surgery with observation; chemotherapy is generally not recommended.
bullets: Curative resection already performed; no adjuvant chemotherapy
Shared decision-making: for high-risk pMMR only, single-agent capecitabine may be discussed (modest, uncertain benefit)
Proceed to surveillance

nodes.name: Stage II high-risk adjuvant
nodes.title: Stage II colon, high-risk pMMR: adjuvant chemotherapy
nodes.description: High-risk, mismatch-repair-proficient stage II colon cancer: consider adjuvant fluoropyrimidine, with oxaliplatin for the highest-risk features (e.g. T4).
bullets: Fluoropyrimidine alone (infusional 5-FU/leucovorin or capecitabine) for high-risk disease without T4
Add oxaliplatin (FOLFOX or CAPOX) for T4 or multiple high-risk features
Duration up to ~6 months; weigh oxaliplatin neurotoxicity against small absolute benefit
Regimens referenced below; the dose engine computes patient doses

nodes.name: Stage III adjuvant
nodes.title: Stage III colon: adjuvant oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy
nodes.description: Node-positive colon cancer: adjuvant oxaliplatin-doublet chemotherapy is standard curative-intent therapy; duration is individualized by risk (IDEA).
bullets: FOLFOX or CAPOX is the standard adjuvant backbone
IDEA duration: 3 months of CAPOX reasonable for low-risk (T1-3 N1); 6 months for high-risk (T4 or N2)
Fluoropyrimidine alone (no oxaliplatin) for patients unfit for oxaliplatin or with pre-existing neuropathy
Biologics (bevacizumab, anti-EGFR) have NO role in the adjuvant setting
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Rectal workup
nodes.title: Rectal: workup
nodes.description: Local T and N staging by pelvic MRI is the pivotal step that determines whether neoadjuvant therapy is needed.
bullets: History and physical with digital rectal exam; rigid or flexible proctoscopy to measure distance from the anal verge
Colonoscopy with biopsy; CEA
Pelvic MRI (preferred) for T stage, mesorectal nodes, circumferential resection margin, and extramural vascular invasion
CT chest / abdomen / pelvis to exclude distant disease
Universal MMR/MSI testing; extended molecular panel if metastatic

nodes.name: Rectal stage
nodes.title: Rectal: clinical stage / risk
nodes.description: Clinical stage on MRI stratifies rectal cancer into early disease (surgery first) versus locally advanced disease (neoadjuvant first) versus metastatic.

tables.title: Rectal cancer: clinical risk groups and default sequencing
rows: Upfront TME (or local excision for select cT1)
cT3-4 and/or N+, or threatened CRM
Total neoadjuvant therapy or neoadjuvant chemoRT, then surgery

nodes.name: Early rectal
nodes.title: Early rectal (cT1-2 N0): surgery first
nodes.description: Clinically early rectal cancer is resected upfront; adjuvant therapy depends on final pathology.
bullets: Transanal local excision for highly selected cT1 N0 with favorable features; otherwise transabdominal total mesorectal excision (TME)
If final pathology is upstaged (pT3-4 or node-positive), give postoperative chemoRT + chemotherapy (or manage as locally advanced)
Proceed to surveillance

nodes.name: LARC neoadjuvant
nodes.title: Locally advanced rectal: neoadjuvant approach
nodes.description: Locally advanced rectal cancer is treated with neoadjuvant therapy before TME. Total neoadjuvant therapy (all chemo + RT before surgery) improves compliance and enables organ preservation.
bullets: Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT): long-course chemoRT (or short-course RT) plus consolidation/induction FOLFOX or CAPOX, then TME
Neoadjuvant chemoRT alone (capecitabine-sensitized long-course RT), then TME, then adjuvant chemotherapy
Selective non-radiation strategy (neoadjuvant FOLFOX alone) for lower-risk cT3 N0/N1 tumors with clear CRM

nodes.name: Rectal TNT
nodes.title: Rectal TNT: all systemic + RT before surgery
nodes.description: Total neoadjuvant therapy delivers radiation and full-course chemotherapy before TME, then response is reassessed.
bullets: Long-course chemoRT (capecitabine-sensitized) or short-course RT (5 x 5 Gy), sequenced with FOLFOX or CAPOX (induction or consolidation)
For dMMR/MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer, neoadjuvant immunotherapy (PD-1 blockade) can produce high complete-response rates - refer to the metastatic dMMR leaf for the agent
Reassess response at completion before committing to surgery vs organ preservation
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Rectal chemoRT
nodes.title: Rectal neoadjuvant chemoRT then adjuvant
nodes.description: Capecitabine-sensitized long-course chemoRT, then TME, then adjuvant chemotherapy to complete perioperative treatment.
bullets: Long-course pelvic RT with concurrent capecitabine (radiosensitizer)
TME ~8-12 weeks after chemoRT
Adjuvant FOLFOX or CAPOX to complete ~6 months of perioperative chemotherapy
Reassess response before surgery
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Rectal reassessment
nodes.title: Rectal: response reassessment after neoadjuvant
nodes.description: After neoadjuvant therapy, restage (DRE, endoscopy, pelvic MRI) to decide between TME and protocolized organ preservation.
bullets: Clinical complete response (cCR): no visible/palpable tumor, normal MRI/endoscopy - candidate for watch-and-wait
Residual disease: proceed to total mesorectal excision

nodes.name: Watch-and-wait
nodes.title: Rectal cCR: organ preservation (watch-and-wait)
nodes.description: Nonoperative management with intensive surveillance after a clinical complete response, preserving the rectum.
bullets: Strict protocolized surveillance: DRE + endoscopy every 3-4 months and pelvic MRI for the first 2-3 years
Salvage TME on any local regrowth (usually still curable)
Reserve for informed patients able to comply with intensive follow-up
Proceed to standard surveillance in parallel

nodes.name: Rectal TME
nodes.title: Rectal residual disease: total mesorectal excision
nodes.description: Residual tumor after neoadjuvant therapy is resected with total mesorectal excision; complete any planned adjuvant chemotherapy.
bullets: Total mesorectal excision (low anterior or abdominoperineal resection) to negative CRM
Complete adjuvant FOLFOX/CAPOX if not fully delivered pre-op (TNT often completes chemotherapy before surgery)
Proceed to surveillance

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Surveillance after curative therapy
nodes.description: Structured follow-up after curative-intent resection to detect recurrence while still salvageable.
bullets: History, physical, and CEA every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6 months to 5 years
CT chest / abdomen / pelvis annually (more often for higher-risk stage III) for up to 5 years
Colonoscopy at 1 year (or ~6 months post-op if not cleared pre-op), then per findings; every 3-5 years thereafter
A rising CEA or new symptom triggers restaging
If recurrence is detected, enter the recurrence pathway
nodes.linkLabel: If recurrence is detected: go to the Recurrence pathway

nodes.name: Recurrence type
nodes.title: Recurrence: pattern
nodes.description: Distinguish isolated locoregional or oligometastatic recurrence (potentially curable with surgery) from widespread metastatic disease.
bullets: Biopsy to confirm recurrence; obtain / update full molecular panel (MMR, RAS, BRAF, HER2)
Restage with CT +/- PET-CT; liver MRI if liver-limited disease is suspected

nodes.name: Locoregional recurrence
nodes.title: Isolated locoregional recurrence
nodes.description: Resectable isolated locoregional recurrence is managed with curative intent.
bullets: Multidisciplinary review for resection; re-irradiation for pelvic recurrence if not previously irradiated
Perioperative systemic chemotherapy around resection
If unresectable or multifocal, manage as metastatic disease
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Metastatic workup
nodes.title: Metastatic: molecular workup
nodes.description: Metastatic colorectal therapy is biomarker-driven. Complete the full molecular panel and assess resectability before selecting first-line therapy.
bullets: MMR/MSI (dMMR/MSI-H predicts immunotherapy benefit)
Extended RAS (KRAS/NRAS exons 2/3/4) and BRAF-V600E
HER2 (ERBB2) amplification / overexpression
Primary tumor sidedness (left = splenic flexure to rectum; right = cecum to transverse)
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis; liver MRI and multidisciplinary review if liver- or lung-limited disease may be resectable

nodes.name: Resectability
nodes.title: Metastatic: resectability
nodes.description: Liver- or lung-limited oligometastatic disease may be curable with metastasectomy; widespread disease is treated with palliative systemic therapy.

nodes.name: Metastasectomy
nodes.title: Resectable metastases: perioperative chemo + metastasectomy
nodes.description: Curative-intent resection of liver- or lung-limited metastases, framed by perioperative chemotherapy.
bullets: Perioperative FOLFOX (about 3 months pre and 3 months post) around metastasectomy, or upfront resection then adjuvant chemotherapy
R0 metastasectomy of liver / lung disease; two-stage or staged resection as needed
Convert borderline-resectable disease with intensive first-line therapy (see biomarker leaves), then re-evaluate for resection
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below
nodes.linkLabel: After curative metastasectomy, resume standard surveillance

nodes.name: Metastatic MMR
nodes.title: Metastatic: MMR / MSI status
nodes.description: Deficient MMR / MSI-high metastatic disease is treated with first-line immunotherapy; proficient MMR disease is chemotherapy-based and directed by RAS/BRAF/HER2 and sidedness.

nodes.name: Metastatic dMMR
nodes.title: Metastatic dMMR/MSI-H: first-line immunotherapy
nodes.description: First-line PD-1 blockade is preferred for deficient-MMR / MSI-high metastatic colorectal cancer and outperforms chemotherapy.
bullets: Single-agent pembrolizumab (PD-1 blockade) is preferred first-line (KEYNOTE-177)
Nivolumab +/- ipilimumab is an alternative immunotherapy option
Reserve chemotherapy for immunotherapy-refractory disease
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Metastatic molecular
nodes.title: Metastatic pMMR: RAS / BRAF / HER2
nodes.description: For proficient-MMR metastatic disease, actionable drivers (BRAF-V600E, HER2 amplification) and RAS status direct targeted therapy layered on a chemotherapy backbone.

nodes.name: Metastatic BRAF-V600E
nodes.title: Metastatic BRAF-V600E
nodes.description: BRAF-V600E confers a poor prognosis; targeted BRAF/EGFR blockade is used after first-line chemotherapy.
bullets: First line: chemotherapy backbone (FOLFOX / FOLFIRI or FOLFOXIRI) +/- bevacizumab
Second line and beyond: encorafenib + cetuximab (BRAF + EGFR blockade); no dose protocol here - describe agents only
Anti-EGFR monotherapy is ineffective in BRAF-V600E disease
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Metastatic HER2+
nodes.title: Metastatic HER2-amplified (RAS wild-type)
nodes.description: HER2 amplification is an actionable target in RAS wild-type metastatic disease, typically after first-line chemotherapy.
bullets: First line: standard chemotherapy backbone +/- bevacizumab
HER2-directed therapy for RAS wild-type disease: trastuzumab + tucatinib, trastuzumab + pertuzumab/lapatinib, or trastuzumab deruxtecan (no dose protocol here - agents only)
Avoid anti-EGFR antibodies in HER2-amplified tumors (predict poor benefit)
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Metastatic RAS-mutant
nodes.title: Metastatic RAS-mutant: chemo + bevacizumab
nodes.description: RAS-mutant disease is not a candidate for anti-EGFR therapy; use a chemotherapy doublet with bevacizumab.
bullets: FOLFOX / CAPOX or FOLFIRI + bevacizumab first line (FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab for fit, high-tumor-burden patients)
NO anti-EGFR antibody (ineffective / harmful in RAS-mutant disease)
Bevacizumab is added as guidance (no dose protocol here); chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Sidedness
nodes.title: Metastatic RAS/BRAF wild-type: primary sidedness
nodes.description: In RAS/BRAF wild-type disease, primary tumor sidedness selects the first-line biologic: anti-EGFR for left-sided primaries, bevacizumab for right-sided.

nodes.name: Left RAS-wt anti-EGFR
nodes.title: Left-sided RAS/BRAF wild-type: chemo + anti-EGFR
nodes.description: Left-sided RAS/BRAF wild-type disease derives the greatest benefit from anti-EGFR antibodies added to a chemotherapy doublet.
bullets: FOLFOX or FOLFIRI + an anti-EGFR antibody (cetuximab or panitumumab) first line
Anti-EGFR is guidance only (no dose protocol here); chemotherapy backbone referenced below
Bevacizumab + doublet is an acceptable alternative

nodes.name: Right RAS-wt bevacizumab
nodes.title: Right-sided RAS/BRAF wild-type: chemo + bevacizumab
nodes.description: Right-sided primaries respond poorly to anti-EGFR therapy; a chemotherapy doublet with bevacizumab is preferred first line.
bullets: FOLFOX / CAPOX or FOLFIRI + bevacizumab first line
Anti-EGFR is less effective for right-sided tumors and is not preferred here
Bevacizumab is guidance only (no dose protocol here); chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Later-line metastatic
nodes.title: Metastatic: later-line / refractory therapy
nodes.description: On progression, sequence the alternate chemotherapy backbone and biologics, then move to refractory oral agents; maintain best supportive care throughout.
bullets: Switch backbone: FOLFIRI if FOLFOX first, or FOLFOX if FOLFIRI first, continuing / switching the biologic by RAS status
Anti-EGFR (RAS wild-type) may be introduced in later lines if not used earlier
Refractory disease: regorafenib or trifluridine-tipiracil (+/- bevacizumab); fruquintinib as a further option - agents only, no dose protocol here
Continue best supportive care; enroll in a clinical trial where available
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below
